README가 'The PR tasks mvcc-lsm-compaction and embedding-drift-monitor are derived from Terminal-Bench ... Their upstream Apache 2.0 license is provided in UPSTREAM_LICENSE'라고 밝히듯, Terminal-Bench에서 가져온 PR 과제 2개의 상류 라이선스입니다. 23개 과제 전체와 오라클, 스크립트에 적용되는 라이선스 문구는 README와 PDF 어디에도 없으므로 (a) 형식의 인용도 만들 수 없습니다. 따라서 라이선스, 상업적 이용, 수정·파생, 재배포의 4개 필드는 어느 증거 형식으로도 채울 수 없습니다. 코드·과제 저장소의 라이선스를 데이터 라이선스로 간주해서도 안 됩니다. 저자가 저장소 전체에 라이선스를 표기하거나 LICENSE 파일의 적용 범위를 밝히는 것이 확인되면 다시 제안해야 합니다. 그때까지 공개할 변경은 없습니다.

screening.paper_title: HarnessSecurity-Bench: Do Security Mechanisms Really Protect Coding Agent Harnesses?
screening.abstract: Coding agent harnesses mediate tool use and authorize actions, yet their security mechanisms and runtime effects remain incompletely characterized. We present HarnessSecurity, the first systematic empirical study and benchmark of open- and closed-source coding agent harnesses. First, we derive a ten-mechanism taxonomy and then assess 400 harness-mechanism cells using independent ratings by researchers and large language model (LLM) judges. We find that about half of confirmed mechanism implementations are opt-in, while closed-source harnesses exhibit substantial evidence gaps. Second, we introduce HarnessSecurity-Bench, a benchmark of 23 tasks across five attack surfaces without sacrificing legitimate task requirements. Using separate deterministic oracles to measure task utility and attack effects with security setting comparisons, we evaluate nine mechanisms across six leading harnesses: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, gptme, Qwen Code, and GitHub Copilot. Under a controlled LLM baseline GLM-5.2, we conduct 2,500 trials, recording 81,155 tool calls and over 2.2 billion tokens. Enabling auto-approve increases utility and raises attack success from 29.2% to 95.6%. Network isolation and read-only mode reduce attack effects with substantial utility losses, while command allowlisting and command denylisting reduce attack effects with a small utility loss and a utility gain, respectively. Task-level cases show that restrictions on a shared capability can obstruct both legitimate and malicious operations, and that allowed tools or commands can leave unauthorized operations reachable through alternative execution paths. Harness providers should make security settings verifiable, test alternative execution paths to protected operations, and assess attack effects alongside task utility and execution costs.
